parts.visual:
Why do people spend 4 hours a day on an app? Because product designers use psychological tricks stolen from casino slot machines.

The Mechanics:
1. Gamification: Applying video game mechanics (points, badges, leaderboards) to non-game environments (like banking apps or fitness trackers).
2. Variable Rewards: You don't know exactly what you will get when you pull to refresh your feed. This uncertainty triggers massive dopamine releases in the human brain.
3. The Habit Loop: Cue, Routine, Reward.
parts.audio: Gamification uses psychological mechanics from video games to drive user engagement. By implementing points, leaderboards, and Variable Rewards, companies manipulate dopamine to create highly addictive products.

questions.question: A language learning app gives you a 'Flame Icon' that burns out if you don't log in for 24 hours. If you lose your 'Streak', you have to start over. What psychological lever are they pulling?
options: Loss Aversion. The human brain hates losing something it has earned more than it likes gaining something new. Users will log in just to avoid the pain of losing their streak.
questions.correct_answer: Loss Aversion. The human brain hates losing something it has earned more than it likes gaining something new. Users will log in just to avoid the pain of losing their streak.
questions.explanation: Streaks are one of the most powerful retention mechanics ever invented in Silicon Valley.

questions.question: Listen to the Product Manager. What mechanism makes social media feeds addictive?
questions.tts_text: When the user pulls down to refresh the page, they don't know if they will see an amazing viral video, or something boring. It's exactly like pulling the lever on a slot machine.
options: Variable Reward Schedules. Unpredictability is highly addictive to the human dopamine system.
questions.correct_answer: Variable Reward Schedules. Unpredictability is highly addictive to the human dopamine system.
questions.explanation: If a reward is 100% predictable, the brain gets bored. If the reward is random, the brain becomes obsessed.

questions.question: What is the dark side of Gamification in the 'Gig Economy' (like delivery apps)?
options: Using game mechanics (like 'Quests' or 'Badges') to trick independent contractors into working dangerous hours for low pay without officially demanding it as an employer.
questions.correct_answer: Using game mechanics (like 'Quests' or 'Badges') to trick independent contractors into working dangerous hours for low pay without officially demanding it as an employer.
questions.explanation: This is algorithmic management. Manipulating behavior through digital rewards instead of traditional wages.

questions.question: What is the 'Habit Loop'?
options: A psychological pattern consisting of a Cue (a notification), a Routine (opening the app), and a Reward (seeing a funny video), which creates a permanent behavioral habit.
questions.correct_answer: A psychological pattern consisting of a Cue (a notification), a Routine (opening the app), and a Reward (seeing a funny video), which creates a permanent behavioral habit.
questions.explanation: Nir Eyal famously documented this in his book 'Hooked'. It is the blueprint for modern product design.

pairs.match: The application of typical elements of game playing to other areas of activity
A cognitive bias where the pain of losing is psychologically twice as powerful as the pleasure of gaining
A schedule of reinforcement where a response is rewarded after an unpredictable amount of time
The neurological pattern that governs any habit (Cue, Routine, Reward)
